title: Joins and grouping
goal: Explain join multiplicity and preserve customers without requests.
prerequisites: onec.p6; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Explain join multiplicity and preserve customers without requests.
sections: A customer with two requests yields two joined rows. Joining another two detail rows can produce four. Aggregating that multiplication is wrong even when syntax is valid. Draw 1: Nrelationships and define result granularity before writing the query: customer, request or document line.

Every query starts with a set specification:row granularity, required fields, scope, identities and multiplicity. Reconcile a small source set manually. Syntax correctness cannot detect lost customers or multiplied sums. Inspect identities and types before totals, which may match accidentally when two defects compensate. Keep this independent oracle beside every query revision.

A left join preserves all customers. Missing right-side fields areNULL, not an empty reference orUndefined. AWHEREcondition on the right table can discard these rows and defeat the intended behavior. Place conditions according to meaning rather than brevity.

Parameters separate structure/values without defining business meaning automatically. References, names and external codes differ. Dates carry time and agreed boundaries. Choose dynamic fields from a structural allowlist, not user text. Specify each parameter’s type, empty-value policy and an example yielding zero rows without changing data. This tests the contract rather than parser acceptance alone.

GROUPBYCustomer collapses documents into customer totals. Name and reference differ: grouping by name can merge distinct customers. DISTINCTis not a universal cure for a bad join; it can hide the defect and discard legitimate equal rows. Fix relationships and aggregation granularity.

Joins and aggregation affect multiplicity differently. Joining two detail sets can multiply rows; grouping can hide the cause behind one wrong sum. Inspect intermediate membership before resources. Respect virtual-table semantics/parameters and temporary-table context/lifetime. Neither mechanism is a universal optimization trick. Explain which problem it solves and verify equivalent values before measuring speed.

UseAlpha with 30/45, Beta with 15, andGamma without requests. Expect 75, 15, and agreed zero/missing resource. Add another customer with the same name but a different reference. Reconcile identities and raw joined rows to detect lost empty groups and accidental merging.

Compare performance only after equivalence. Freeze data, versions, call count, cache conditions and repeated timing. A small local experiment does not establish field p95. Reject speedups caused by dropped rows or permission checks. Preserve rejected variants, reasons and the correct baseline so later optimization does not repeat a known defect. Report observed metrics without broadening their scope.
